project_scope.selection_mode: modern broad family with local Yucca visual anchor
project_scope.note: The modern family is heterogeneous; do not use the Yucca rosette as a universal family definition.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: For local Yucca, start with rosette/trunk architecture and the true fibrous leaves. Inspect terminal spine/margin fibers, then the terminal panicle with 3+3 tepals and the fruit.
family_diagnostics.broad_family: Modern Asparagaceae is morphologically broad; reproductive characters commonly include 6 tepals, 6 stamens and a 3-locular ovary, but ovary position and fruit type vary.
family_diagnostics.local_yucca: Stiff fibrous leaves in rosettes or on trunks; large terminal flower panicles; 6 fleshy tepals; 6 stamens; 3-carpellate fruit.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Yucca has true leaves and no cactus areoles. Use leaf texture/armature plus flower/fruit for species.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → diagnostic structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: The local lesson is really 'how to read Yucca' while remembering that Yucca is only one form inside broad Asparagaceae.

steps.title: 1 · Read the rosette
steps.look_for: Basal/terminal cluster of true fibrous leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Yucca from superficially spiny cacti and begins the species comparison.

steps.title: 2 · Inspect the leaf
steps.look_for: Leaf stiffness, twist, color, marginal threads and terminal spine.
steps.why_it_matters: Vegetative Yucca ID often starts here.

steps.title: 3 · Compare a narrow-leaved species
steps.look_for: Narrower flexible leaves and different margin/fiber pattern.
steps.why_it_matters: Builds a useful local Yucca contrast before flowering.

steps.title: 4 · Add trunked architecture
steps.look_for: Arborescent/trunked habit with stout rosettes and strongly armed leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows how much vegetative architecture varies within local Yucca.

steps.title: 5 · Confirm the flower/fruit
steps.look_for: Large terminal panicle, six tepals and 3-carpellate fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: Reproductive characters confirm the local genus/family placement.

comparisons.title: Yucca vs Cactaceae
comparisons.rule: Yucca has true fibrous leaves in a rosette and lacks areoles. Cacti have specialized areoles and highly modified/reduced leaves.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not generalize Yucca's rosette/spines to all modern Asparagaceae.
